edition.copy_text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI

source_text: Νοείσθωσαν τοίνυν πάντες οἱ ἐπὶ γῆς μιᾷ τινι διαλέκτῳ θείᾳ χρώμενοι, καὶ ὅσον γε συμφωνοῦσι πρὸς ἀλλήλους τηρείσθωσαν ἐν τῇ θείᾳ διαλέκτῳ· καὶ ἔστωσαν ἀκίνητοι „τῶν ἀνατολῶν.“ ἐς ὅσον εἰσὶ τὰ τοῦ φωτὸς καὶ τοῦ ἀπὸ „φωτὸς ἀϊδίου“ ἀπαυγάσματος φρονοῦντες. καὶ οὗτοι, ἐπὰν κινήσωσιν „ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνατολῶν“ ἑαυτοὺς ἀλλότρια „ἀνατολῶν“ φρονοῦντες, εὑρισκέτωσαν „πεδίον ἐν γῇ Σενναὰρ,“ ὅπερ ἑρμηνεύεται ὀδόντων ἐκτιναγμὸς κατὰ σύμβολον τοῦ ἀπολλύναι αὐτοὺς τὰ δι᾿ ὧν τρέφονται, καὶ κατοικείτωσαν ἐκεῖ. εἶτα τὰ τῆς ὕλης συναγαγεῖν θέλοντες καὶ κολλᾶν τὰ μὴ πεφυκότα κολλᾶσθαι οὐρανῷ, ἵνα διὰ τῶν ὑλικῶν ἐπιβουλεύσωσι τοῖς ἀΰλοις, λεγέτωσαν· „δεῦτε πλινθεύσωμεν πλίνθους καὶ ὀπτήσωμεν αὐτὰς πυρί.“ ὡς οὖν κρατύνοντες καὶ πηγνύντες τὰ πήλινα καὶ ὑλικὰ καὶ τὴν πλίνθον λίθον ποιεῖν θέλοντες καὶ τὸν πηλὸν ἄσφαλτον καὶ διὰ τούτων οἰκοδομεῖν „πόλιν καὶ πύργον, οὗ“ ὅσον ἐπὶ τῇ ὑπολήψει αὐτῶν „ἔσται ἡ κεφαλὴ ἕως τοῦ οὐρανοῦ“ κατὰ τὰ ὑπεραιρόμενα ὑψώματα κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ , παραδιδόσθωσαν ἕκαστος κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆς „ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν“ κινήσεως, ἐπὶ πλεῖον ἢ ἐπ᾿ ἔλαττον αὐτοῖς γεγενημένης, καὶ κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆς κατασκευῆς τῶν πλίνθων εἰς λίθους καὶ τοῦ πηλοῦ εἰς ἄσφαλτον καὶ τῆς ἐκ τούτων οἰκοδομῆς ἀγγέλοις, ἐπὶ πλεῖον ἢ ἐπ᾿ ἔλαττον χαλεπωτέροις καὶ τοιοῖσδε ἢ τοιοῖσδε, ἕως τίσωσι δίκας ἐφ᾿ οἷς τετολμήκασι· καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων ἀγέσθωσαν ἕκαστος τῶν ἐμποιησάντων τὴν οἰκείαν ἑαυτοῖς διάλεκτον ἐπὶ τὰ μέρη τῆς γῆς κατὰ τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀξίαν, οἵδε μὲν ἐπὶ τὴν φέρ᾿ εἰπεῖν καυσώδη χώραν ἄλλοι δ᾿ ἐπὶ τὴν διὰ τὸ κατεψῦχθαι κολάζουσαν τοὺς ἐνοικοῦντας, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐπὶ τὴν δυσγεωργητοτέραν ἄλλοι δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἔλαττον τοιαύτην, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐπὶ τὴν πεπληρωμένην θηρίων οἱ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἔλαττον ἔχουσαν αὐτά.
thought_title: Leaving the east and building the tower
pass_a_gloss: Let all those on earth then be thought of (νοέω) as using one divine language (θεία διάλεκτος), and so long as they are in concord (συμφωνέω) with one another let them be kept (τηρέω) in the divine language; and let them be unmoved (ἀκίνητος) from 'the east', so long as they are minding (φρονέω) the things of the light and of the radiance (ἀπαύγασμα) from 'eternal light (φῶς ἀΐδιον)'. And these, when they move (κινέω) themselves 'from the east', minding things foreign (ἀλλότρια) to 'the east', let them find 'a plain in the land of Sennaar', which is interpreted (ἑρμηνεύω) 'shaking out of teeth (ὀδόντων ἐκτιναγμός)', as a symbol (σύμβολον) of their losing (ἀπόλλυμι) the things by which they are nourished (τρέφω), and let them dwell there. Then, wishing to gather (συνάγω) the things of matter (ὕλη) and to glue (κολλάω) things not naturally fit to be glued to heaven, so that through material things (ὑλικά) they may plot against (ἐπιβουλεύω) the immaterial (ἄϋλα), let them say: 'Come, let us make bricks (πλινθεύω) and bake them with fire.' So, as strengthening (κρατύνω) and making solid (πήγνυμι) the clay and material things, and wishing to make the brick stone and the clay (πηλός) bitumen (ἄσφαλτος), and through these to build 'a city and tower, whose' as far as their supposition (ὑπόληψις) goes 'head will be up to heaven', according to the exalted heights (ὑπεραιρόμενα ὑψώματα) against the knowledge (γνῶσις) of God, let them be handed over (παραδίδωμι) each, according to the proportion (ἀναλογία) of the movement 'from the east', having happened to them more or less, and according to the proportion of the preparation of bricks into stones and of clay into bitumen and of the building from these, to angels more or less harsh (χαλεπός) and of this sort or that, until they pay penalty (δίκας τίνω) for what they dared (τολμάω); and by the angels let them be led, each by those who produced in them (ἐμποιέω) their own language, to the parts of the earth according to their worth (ἀξία): some, so to speak, to the scorching (καυσώδης) land, others to the one punishing (κολάζω) its inhabitants by being chilled (καταψύχω), and some to the harder to farm (δυσγεώργητος), others to the less such, and some to the one filled with wild beasts (θηρία), others to the one having fewer of them.

pass_b_english: Let us think of all those on earth, then, as using one divine language; and for as long as they are in harmony with one another, let them be kept in that divine language. And let them remain unmoved from “the east” so long as their minds are set on the things of the light, and of the radiance that comes from “eternal light” (Wisdom of Solomon 7:26). And when these move themselves “from the east,” setting their minds on things foreign to “the east,” let them find “a plain in the land of Shinar” (Genesis 11:2), a name which means “shaking out of teeth,” as a symbol that they lose the things by which they are fed; and let them settle there.

Then, wishing to gather together the things of matter, and to fasten to heaven what by nature cannot be fastened to it, so that by material things they may plot against things that are immaterial, let them say: “Come, let us make bricks and bake them with fire” (Genesis 11:3). So then, as they harden and make solid what is of clay and of matter, and want to make the brick into stone and the clay into bitumen (Genesis 11:3), and by these means to build “a city and a tower whose top,” as far as their own notion goes, “shall reach to heaven” (Genesis 11:4), in the manner of the heights that are lifted up “against the knowledge of God” (2 Corinthians 10:5), let them be handed over, each of them, to angels: angels harsher in a greater or lesser degree, and of one kind or another, in proportion to the movement “from the east” that has taken place in them to a greater or lesser degree, and in proportion to their making bricks into stones and clay into bitumen, and to their building from these, until they pay the penalty for what they have dared.

And let them be led, each of them, by the angels who implanted in them their own language, to the parts of the earth according to what each deserves: some, let us say, to a scorching land, others to a land that punishes those who live in it by its cold; some to a land harder to farm, others to one less so; some to a land full of wild beasts, others to one with fewer of them.
notes: The chapter is an allegory of Genesis 11:1-9 told in third-person imperatives ('let them be thought of ... let them find ... let them be handed over'); kept as 'let ...' to preserve Origen's hypothetical, teaching form. 'Radiance of eternal light' (ἀπαύγασμα φωτὸς ἀϊδίου) is Wisdom of Solomon 7:26 (compare Hebrews 1:3, ἀπαύγασμα; not cited inline). Genesis 11:2-4 quoted from the LXX; Genesis 11:3 LXX has 'the brick became stone for them, and bitumen was their mortar (πηλός)'; Origen turns it into 'make brick into stone and clay into bitumen'. 'Shaking out of teeth' (ὀδόντων ἐκτιναγμός) is Origen's etymology of Shinar (Sennaar), from an onomastic tradition; given as he states it. 'Heights lifted up against the knowledge of God' adapts 2 Corinthians 10:5 (πᾶν ὕψωμα ἐπαιρόμενον κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ); Origen writes ὑπεραιρόμενα ὑψώματα. The staged text shows a stray full stop before ἐς ὅσον and a spaced comma after θεοῦ; read as one sentence each. τῶν ἐμποιησάντων τὴν οἰκείαν ἑαυτοῖς διάλεκτον taken as 'the angels who implanted in them their own language' (i.e. each group's angels gave it its tongue; ἑαυτοῖς most naturally means the angels' own language, and the English 'their own' keeps that open).
